content:
Over the past couple of days, two separate reports have highlighted different ways in which Apple could boost profits by expanding its services business.

In my view, there's one direction Apple absolutely should take, and one that it absolutely should not — and it seems Phil Schiller might even agree with me on this one …

First, a quick recap of the two reports.

Home security and monitoring service

A Bloomberg report on Friday said that Apple plans to launch a brand-new home security and monitoring service, on top of new home hardware products.

Squeezing more money from the App Store

A second report from the same outlet on Sunday said Apple is looking at ways to squeeze more money and profit from the App Store.

Apple should NOT go down the latter path

Let's start with the latter: I believe going in that second direction would be a huge mistake.

Apple's effective monopoly position on iPhone app sales has come in for fierce criticism from regulators around the world. In most countries, if you want to sell an iPhone app, you have to go through the official App Store, and you have no choice but to accept Apple's terms.

I know a lot of people will say nobody is forcing you to buy an iPhone or develop apps for one, but that's not how genuine free-market capitalism works: the US has had anti-monopoly laws since 1890. Once you reach a certain level of market dominance, your behaviour is constrained to prevent you from abusing that position.

Trying to squeeze more money out of the App Store is the exact opposite of the 'skating to where the puck is going' philosophy. Phil Schiller is reported to take the same view, with Bloomberg hinting that this is one of the reasons for his current retirement.

Innovative services is the right direction

By contrast, launching genuinely creative new services that customers are happy to pay for is the direction Apple should be taking. I can absolutely see the value of Apple offering a home security monitoring service.

I said back in 2024 that launching an Apple-branded smart home camera would be one of the smartest moves the company could make. I said the same about the long-rumoured Apple smart doorbell. Offering an optional service bundle alongside security products makes perfect sense, for two reasons.

First, there's the privacy consideration I've mentioned many times before. HomeKit Secure Video already does a lot to protect the privacy of security camera footage. If I had to pick one company to carry out AI analysis of my security camera footage, I'd pick Apple.

Second, Apple is best placed to fully integrate security hardware and services into the HomeKit ecosystem. I believe there are many other areas where Apple could offer a similar edge.

For me, the point is that Apple needs to apply to services the same attitude it applies to hardware. Make a great product, and people will happily and willingly part with their money. Not by squeezing cash in ways that leave customers, developers, and regulators unhappy.

What do you think? Please share your views in the comments.
